title: Domain values, bounded state, local storage and diagnostics

files.role: Separates a concrete input identity from a capture-mode choice, so Both is not mistaken for a third transcript source.

blocks.title: Two byte-valued sources, three selection modes
blocks.explanation: AudioSource explicitly assigns Computer=1 and Microphone=2 with byte storage; zero is not a declared source. AudioCaptureMode is a separate enum whose Both value selects inputs rather than labeling one segment. Keeping the types separate prevents source provenance from becoming an ambiguous mixed-track label. These declarations do not open either device.

blocks.title: Stable wire names and human labels with rejecting defaults
blocks.explanation: WireName maps only the two valid inputs to lowercase protocol tokens; DisplayName uses Computer and Mic for presentation. Both switch defaults throw rather than silently reinterpret an unknown numeric value. The label names identify capture inputs, not people or diarized speakers, and transcript identity must never be recovered by parsing these labels.

files.role: Provides a bounded local JSONL writer and a separate metadata-first facade with explicit content opt-in, observable drops and generic I/O failure reporting.

blocks.title: Typed events and a record capable of holding optional content
blocks.explanation: Imports supply clocks, UTF-8, JSON and channels. DiagnosticEvent names lifecycle, audio, transcript, question and answer milestones; DiagnosticContent limits the facade's content categories to final transcript, submitted question and answer. DiagnosticRecord carries UTC and monotonic clocks, process ID, correlation/related IDs, optional elapsed/count values and optional strings. Text is possible in the raw record: the record type itself neither redacts nor requires opt-in. LoggingDropped is declared here but the writer below increments a counter rather than emitting that event automatically.

blocks.title: Create a bounded channel and one background drain
blocks.explanation: The writer retains a full directory path, rotation settings, channel/task and interlocked or volatile status fields. Filenames include UTC time, process ID and a GUID to distinguish logger instances. Defaults are 2,097,152 bytes per file, ten files and 1,024 queued records; guards require at least 1,024 bytes, two files and one slot. SingleReader=true matches one WriteAsync consumer. FullMode.Wait does not make the public TryWrite block: it makes a full channel reject that non-waiting call. Capacity counts record objects, not their aggregate memory or UTF-8 bytes.

blocks.title: Never wait for capacity on the producer path
blocks.explanation: TryWrite rejects null synchronously. A disposed writer or unsuccessful channel TryWrite increments dropped atomically and returns false; accepted enqueue returns true, not proof of eventual disk persistence. A producer racing disposal may be rejected by the completed channel. No privacy or record-size validation happens here, so callers bypassing LocalDiagnostics can submit arbitrary DiagnosticRecord.Text.

blocks.title: Serialize, measure bytes, rotate, append and report failures
blocks.explanation: The single reader creates the directory for each record and rejects a reparse-point attribute on that directory. It serializes before measuring UTF-8 bytes, including the platform newline; an oversized record is dropped with record_limit without appending. Rotation occurs before an append that would exceed the current file limit. BOM-free append is followed by Prune, then failureCode is cleared on success. IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException increment drops, set diagnostic_io and emit a generic Trace message without the exception body. If append succeeds but pruning fails, the drop count still increases although the record may exist on disk. Other exceptions are not caught by this filter; this is neither universal fault suppression nor a race-free filesystem security sandbox.

blocks.title: Retention, bounded shutdown wait and JSON representation
blocks.explanation: Prune enumerates events-*.jsonl across the directory, excludes reparse-point files and this instance's current file, orders the rest by newest LastWriteTimeUtc and deletes everything beyond maximumFiles-1. Thus retention is not scoped to the instance identity; concurrent writers or skipped links are outside a strict directory-wide size guarantee. Dispose is idempotent via Interlocked.Exchange, completes the channel and waits at most three seconds for draining. Timeout sets flush_timeout but does not cancel the drain. A faulted writer can make Wait throw. JSON omits null fields and serializes enums as strings.

blocks.title: Lazy local sink and fail-closed text settings
blocks.explanation: Paths live under LocalApplicationData/PhantomFudge; inspecting failure/drop properties does not create the Lazy sink. ReloadSettings first disables text, then treats a missing file as metadata-only. It rejects files longer than 1,024 bytes and requires a JSON object with exactly one property named includeText whose value is Boolean. Extra or duplicate properties therefore fail the count check. Only after successful parsing is text enabled. Parse/open errors propagate to the application handler; resetting first prevents a previously enabled value surviving a failed reload. This checks stream length before parsing, not a locked immutable settings snapshot.

blocks.title: Validate metadata before instantiating the sink
blocks.explanation: Record accepts defined events, nonnegative optional elapsed/count values, SafeCode-compatible codes and a fixed provider allowlist. Invalid input throws before Sink.Value is accessed. Accepted records receive fresh UTC, Stopwatch ticks and process ID; relatedId permits a second correlation. TryWrite's Boolean result is deliberately not returned, so health is observed through dropped/failure properties. SafeCode constrains syntax and length, not semantic secrecy: an allowed single-word string is not automatically safe to log.

blocks.title: Explicitly enabled content has a separate truncation policy
blocks.explanation: RecordContent validates null and enum input even when text logging is disabled, then returns without creating a sink unless includeText is true. It maps the three content kinds onto transcript-final, question-frozen and answer-completed events. Count records the original .NET string length; Text keeps at most 32,768 UTF-16 code units, with content_opt_in or content_truncated marking the decision. This is not byte-based or grapheme-aware truncation and can split a surrogate pair. Serialized-byte limits are applied later by JsonlDiagnosticLog.

blocks.title: Exception identity and bounded sanitized stack frames
blocks.explanation: RecordException sends the exception type name through Record, never error.Message or ToString. It follows at most four InnerException levels and takes at most eight frames from each StackTrace constructed without file information. Declaring-type and method names are joined, non-ASCII/non-allowed punctuation is replaced with underscores, and the result is capped at 96 characters. Depth is recorded as Count. This preserves structural failure clues without paths or arguments, but unusual exception type names can fail Record's SafeCode validation and method names remain metadata rather than content redaction.

blocks.title: Stop only an existing sink and constrain metadata tokens
blocks.explanation: FlushAndStop does not instantiate a logger just to shut it down. It disposes the existing Lazy value and does not replace it, so later valid records target that disposed sink and are counted as drops. SafeCode permits null or a 1..96-character ASCII alphanumeric token plus underscore, hyphen, period and colon; empty strings, spaces, slashes and arbitrary Unicode are rejected. The facade is a controlled logging API, not an encryption or authorization mechanism.

files.role: Turns bounded palette text into allowlisted command data and offers curated prefixes without executing actions, shell syntax or model requests.

blocks.title: Separate command identity, payload and curated examples
blocks.explanation: KeyboardCommandKind declares seventeen action families including Context; KeyboardCommand carries optional Argument or Value data. Its constructor is not the validation boundary: Parse supplies that contract. Input is capped at128 units, font at8..24, and the read-only twenty-five examples include context on/off plus record aliases. Creating command data never starts recording, sends a question, copies text or changes a window.

blocks.title: Accept exactly one built-in token pattern
blocks.explanation: Parse first tokenizes and gives an empty token list its own authored error. Exact list patterns enforce argument count: start and record start produce the same Start value, while source, clarify and theme accept only their listed normalized arguments. Font and opacity produce integer Value payloads through separate inclusive bounds of 8..24 and 10..100. Everything else, including missing or excess arguments, receives the fixed unknown-command ArgumentException with parameter text rather than an echoed input. Matching returns data, not an invocation; caller-side availability, confirmation and application-state guards are not enforced by this parser. The context token pattern accepts exactly on or off and constructs Context data. It does not accept arbitrary context text, file paths or missing/extra arguments.

blocks.title: Prefix suggestions are neither validation nor completion of every value
blocks.explanation: Suggest uses the same tokenizer as Parse and rejoins normalized tokens with one space. It filters Examples with an ordinal case-insensitive prefix comparison, retains declaration order and clamps maximum to 0..20, defaulting to five. Each call materializes a fresh read-only array wrapper, so later calls cannot mutate an earlier result. Blank input offers the initial examples; an unmatched prefix yields an empty list without invoking Parse. Thus font 8 is valid but has no suggestion because the curated numeric example is font 14. Even a zero result limit still runs tokenizer validation first.

blocks.title: Validate raw text before whitespace and colon normalization
blocks.explanation: Tokenize rejects null, then raw string lengths above 128, then control characters other than tab, CR and LF. The ceiling counts UTF-16 code units including leading/trailing whitespace and any colon, not bytes or visible glyphs. Control validation precedes trimming, so forbidden controls cannot disappear at the edges. Trimming removes surrounding whitespace, at most one leading colon is stripped, and invariant lowercasing plus whitespace splitting produces the command tokens. Unicode whitespace can separate tokens, but control whitespace such as vertical tab remains forbidden. Newlines separate words, not independent commands: source newline mic can match one command, whereas start newline stop cannot.

blocks.title: Reject decorated, overflowing or out-of-range numeric arguments
blocks.explanation: ParseInteger uses int.TryParse with NumberStyles.None and InvariantCulture, then checks both inclusive endpoints before returning a value. Decimal digit strings with leading zeroes are accepted; signs, fractions, exponents, grouping, unit suffixes and Int32 overflow are not coerced or clamped. Both parse and range failures throw the caller-supplied fixed message with parameter text, without copying the numeric input into the error. This helper validates the numeric token only; the list-pattern caller has already enforced the command's two-token shape.

files.role: Loads a small strict local shortcut document and resolves an allowlisted activation key while distinguishing absent settings from malformed or inaccessible settings.

blocks.title: Resolve a key without normalizing stored text or registering a hotkey
blocks.explanation: Settings default to Enabled=true and ActivationKey=K. Both Validate and the computed VirtualKey call the same resolver, even when Enabled is false; record construction alone performs no validation. A one-character ASCII letter is uppercased invariantly and accepted except E. Function keys require F or f, length two or three, no leading zero, invariant unsigned integer syntax and a number from one through eleven, mapping to 0x70..0x7A. F12 and f12 are rejected along with null, whitespace-padded names and Unicode lookalikes; ArgumentException names ActivationKey and advertises only A-Z except E or F1-F11. Stored casing is preserved. This validates a key value, not modifier policy, OS registration availability or successful shortcut activation.

blocks.title: Default only when opening finds no file or directory
blocks.explanation: The loader owns a 1,024-byte ceiling and a UTF-8 decoder configured to throw rather than replace malformed bytes. FilePath is a mutable public field initially pointing to LocalApplicationData/PhantomFudge/keyboard.json; a non-null argument takes precedence, while null uses that field. Opening uses FileMode.Open, read access and FileShare.Read. Only FileNotFoundException and DirectoryNotFoundException return new default settings. No directory or file is created. Invalid paths, access denial and sharing or other I/O failures propagate instead of silently enabling the default shortcut.

blocks.title: Bound bytes before decoding and parsing
blocks.explanation: Within a disposing stream scope, ReadAtLeast requests 1,025 bytes with end-of-stream permitted. A count above 1,024 rejects the file before decoding or JSON parsing; this bounds the read buffer without trusting an initial Length property or reading a huge file in full. A leading three-byte UTF-8 BOM is excluded only from decoding, so it still consumes the byte budget. Invalid UTF-8 is translated into a fixed InvalidDataException. JsonDocument.Parse uses its default strict syntax and its JsonException is not caught. A successfully parsed non-object root gets a separate InvalidDataException; neither failure path rewrites the input.

blocks.title: Reject duplicate, unknown, mis-cased and mistyped properties
blocks.explanation: Property names enter an ordinal HashSet before dispatch, so duplicates are rejected even when different JSON escape spellings decode to the same name. The switch permits only exact schemaVersion, enabled and activationKey names. Version must be a JSON number readable as Int32 and equal to one; enabled must be a JSON Boolean; activationKey must be a JSON string. Unknown names and wrong value kinds fail immediately with fixed InvalidDataException messages. Local initial values are only parsing storage, not permission to omit fields. Enumeration and validation remain inside both disposal scopes.

blocks.title: Require the complete schema before validating and returning
blocks.explanation: Exactly three distinct properties must survive the allowlist, which together with duplicate and unknown-name rejection guarantees that all required names appeared. Missing fields cannot inherit the local enabled or activationKey initializers. Only then does the loader create the settings record and validate the activation key; an invalid key propagates ArgumentException, including for disabled settings, rather than becoming a schema error or default. Each call reads anew and returns only after all checks; there is no last-good cache, automatic repair, persistence or hotkey registration in this file.

files.role: Reads and explicitly writes bounded strict UTF-8 notes, preserving BOM choice and using byte fingerprints to detect observed external changes.

blocks.title: A byte budget, strict encoder and conflict-specific exception
blocks.explanation: NoteSnapshot returns text, BOM presence and a SHA-256 fingerprint; its positional record is an immutable-value style carrier with generated init properties, unlike the getter-only transcript classes. NoteConflictException is an IOException with a generic message. StrictUtf8 uses no automatic BOM and throws on invalid encoding input. Fits measures UTF-8 bytes, subtracting three bytes when a BOM is requested; an unpaired surrogate yields false through EncoderFallbackException. Null is not caught by that filter. The 1 MiB limit is not a character count.

blocks.title: Bound the read while streaming and hash original bytes
blocks.explanation: ReadAsync opens an asynchronous sequential stream with FileShare.ReadWrite, reads 16,384-byte chunks and checks the accumulated byte length before appending each chunk. It therefore rejects growth beyond 1 MiB rather than trusting initial file size. After buffering, it detects a leading UTF-8 BOM, decodes the remaining bytes strictly and hashes the complete bytes including that BOM. Text/newlines are not normalized. Shared access allows concurrent writers; the returned fingerprint describes bytes actually read, not a guaranteed point-in-time filesystem snapshot.

blocks.title: Validate and prepare a same-directory temporary before writing
blocks.explanation: WriteAsync rejects text that does not fit before filesystem mutation; invalid surrogate input is reported with the same InvalidDataException message as overflow. It resolves the target path, chooses a GUID-named .phantom temporary in the target directory, encodes text and explicitly prepends BOM bytes when requested. The first VerifyUnchangedAsync runs before the temporary exists. A null expectedFingerprint means create-only, not permission to overwrite an arbitrary existing file.

blocks.title: Flush, recheck, honor cancellation, publish and clean up
blocks.explanation: CreateNew plus FileShare.None protects the temporary's creation and handle. The code writes bytes, awaits a flush, requests Flush(true), and closes the stream before a second fingerprint check. A cancellation check immediately precedes File.Move; overwrite is enabled only when an expected fingerprint was supplied. The result hashes the exact bytes prepared. Finally deletes any remaining temporary on success or failure. This is optimistic replacement, not compare-and-swap: another writer can change the target after the second check and before Move. Cleanup failures can propagate, and these calls do not establish crash-proof directory-entry durability.

blocks.title: Creation and replacement have different conflict contracts
blocks.explanation: With no expected fingerprint, any existing target is a conflict; otherwise absence is also a conflict, preventing silent recreation of a deleted file. An existing target is reread through the same bounded strict UTF-8 reader and compared with StringComparer.Ordinal. Hashes detect byte differences including BOM changes, not only visual text changes. Access, invalid encoding and oversize failures from ReadAsync can propagate as their own errors instead of NoteConflictException. No lock is held across verification and publication.

files.role: Defines the .NET Core library project without a WPF target or direct package declarations.

blocks.title: Minimal SDK-style net10.0 library
blocks.explanation: Microsoft.NET.Sdk consumes this project and targets net10.0. No OutputType, WPF flag or PackageReference is declared here; shared Directory.Build.props supplies nullable analysis, implicit usings, warnings-as-errors, deterministic builds and lockfile restore settings. This file is the build declaration, not evidence of a successful build or portability of every provider implementation compiled into Core.

files.role: Owns explicitly selected or typed question state, preserves user edits against recognition refresh and freezes an exact local snapshot.

blocks.title: Caller-serialized question state and two independent ceilings
blocks.explanation: A draft starts with a fresh question GUID, revision zero, empty text and a read-only empty selection. Limits are 8,192 .NET string-length units and 256 selected segments, so even zero-length provenance is bounded. IsProvisional means any selected copy is not final; it does not mean currently active capture, and a typed-only draft is not provisional. The class comment requires one serialized caller, normally the UI dispatcher; there is no internal synchronization.

blocks.title: Stage explicit selection without touching committed state
blocks.explanation: ReplaceSelection enumerates into local collections. Null input/items fail, and all entries must belong to one capture session. A HashSet deduplicates by the complete TranscriptSegmentKey while preserving the first occurrence and the caller's order; a later revision with the same key does not silently win. The count guard applies after deduplication. Each accepted segment and key is copied. Cross-session, count and enumeration failures occur before assignments to the draft.

blocks.title: Compose before commit and make explicit replacement reset editing
blocks.explanation: Compose can reject oversized combined text before state changes. Equal text plus value-equal selected records is a no-op only while UserEdited is false. Otherwise checked revision arithmetic is evaluated before publishing the read-only array, text and reset edit flag. Reselecting after a user edit deliberately reenables selected ASR refresh, even if some visible text happens to match. Replacement does not change QuestionId.

blocks.title: Identical text is still an explicit edit
blocks.explanation: EditText validates before mutation and increments Revision only when the string differs exactly. It always sets UserEdited=true, even if the user reasserts the same text. This flag is a policy change independent of numeric revision: subsequent Refresh must not overwrite text or provenance. No trimming, newline rewriting or Unicode normalization occurs, and existing selected copies remain available as original provenance.

blocks.title: Refresh only selected nonfinal keys with newer revisions
blocks.explanation: A null store fails; an edited draft or empty selection returns immediately. Current store records are indexed by full key, and the draft walks its own selection order. Only a previously nonfinal selection with the same current key and strictly greater revision is replaced by a copy; missing/evicted records and selected finals remain unchanged. Value equality avoids revision inflation. Compose and checked arithmetic run before committing, so an oversized ASR update preserves the old text, selection object and revision rather than truncating the question.

blocks.title: Clear identity explicitly and freeze without sending
blocks.explanation: Clear generates a new question GUID, resets revision/text/edit state and drops selected references, preventing late refresh from repopulating an empty selection. Freeze validates the existing text, rejects whitespace-only questions, and constructs a snapshot with the current ID/revision, exact string, source copies and flags plus Stopwatch.GetTimestamp. It neither increments the draft revision nor calls a provider. Repeated freezes can therefore share ID/revision but are distinct snapshot objects with capture-time timestamps.

blocks.title: Count UTF-16 units and only the separators actually emitted
blocks.explanation: ValidateText rejects null and strings longer than 8,192 UTF-16 code units, not bytes or graphemes. Compose skips only zero-length strings, not whitespace strings, and uses a long accumulator. It adds Environment.NewLine.Length only between nonempty segment texts, matching the later string.Join exactly. A replacement overflow is ArgumentException with parameter segments; a refresh overflow is InvalidOperationException describing retained state. The join is delayed until the budget passes, and selected empty records remain in provenance even though they contribute no separators.

files.role: Carries an immutable local question value whose exact text and copied provenance are independent of later draft/store mutations.

blocks.title: Freeze value identity, exact text, provenance and clock together
blocks.explanation: The internal constructor stores the question GUID, draft revision and exact string without rewriting them, deep-copies every TranscriptSegment and its key into a read-only array, and captures provisional/edit flags plus a supplied monotonic timestamp. All exposed properties are getter-only. Strings are immutable, so sharing ExactText is safe; wrapping only the original caller list would not have been enough. Validation belongs to QuestionDraft.Freeze rather than being repeated here. SourceRefs can retain original ASR text after an edit and are local provenance, not a request payload to serialize indiscriminately.

files.role: Maintains a bounded caller-serialized selection model with stable local keys, source epochs, immutable revisions and session-global final deduplication.

blocks.title: Bound retained selection history, not the complete export
blocks.explanation: The store has positive configurable segment and character budgets, defaulting to 256 and 64,000. It tracks latest epochs per source, a list of immutable records, a lifetime local-ID counter and a session-global final-ID high-water mark. Segments returns a newly copied array with a read-only wrapper: membership cannot mutate, while immutable record instances may be shared. SessionId starts empty, requiring BeginSession before valid events are accepted. Caller serialization is a precondition, not a lock implemented here.

blocks.title: Start another session without inventing finals
blocks.explanation: BeginSession rejects an empty GUID, the current GUID and any GUID still present in retained segments. It first constructs a replacement list that closes every active partial by adding a revision while keeping IsFinal false. It then clears epochs, resets the protocol high-water mark and installs the new session ID. Existing finals/history survive and the local-ID counter does not reset. This is not a permanent registry of every GUID ever seen: IDs absent after eviction or Clear cannot be detected by the retained-history check.

blocks.title: Apply partial updates transactionally around a stable key
blocks.explanation: SetPartial validates even before checking whether an event is stale. Obsolete session/epoch returns false. PrepareUpdate stages source-epoch closures, then FindPartial locates the active utterance for that source/epoch. Changed text replaces its record with checked revision+1; identical text preserves revision. A nonempty new utterance allocates a checked local ID and revision one, whereas an empty partial without an existing utterance creates no row. ApplyUpdate must succeed before epoch and ID counters are committed. True means accepted, including unchanged or empty input, not necessarily a visible change.

blocks.title: Settle partials and advance one session-global final mark
blocks.explanation: AddFinal validates source/text/epoch, positive protocol ID and optional timing before rejecting stale events or IDs at/below the global high-water mark. It settles only the matching active source/epoch, retaining the key and incrementing revision even when final text is unchanged or empty. An empty final replaces guessed text with empty, not the prior guess. Without a partial, only nonempty finals create rows. Capacity is applied before counters are changed. The accepted protocol ID advances even for empty finals with no row, keeping duplicate memory constant while relying on in-order, session-global protocol delivery.

blocks.title: Clear callbacks' current session and centralize input guards
blocks.explanation: Clear empties retained rows and epoch/final tracking and sets SessionId to Guid.Empty, but intentionally leaves lastLocalSegmentId intact for this store object's lifetime. Earlier array snapshots retain their contents. ValidateEvent calls session, source, text and epoch guards in that order; malformed obsolete events therefore throw instead of silently returning false. Clearing does not know about QuestionDraft copies and cannot erase them.

blocks.title: Source-specific epoch transitions and unfinished records
blocks.explanation: IsCurrent requires the active session and an epoch not lower than the last accepted epoch for that input. PrepareUpdate closes active records only for the affected source whose epoch differs; a microphone restart does not close Computer. ClosePartial preserves key, text and timing, uses checked revision arithmetic, clears protocol metadata and relies on the default isActive=false without claiming finality. FindPartial uses active/source/epoch fields, not rendered text or a protocol final ID. Old sessions have already had active rows closed by BeginSession.

blocks.title: Evict historical rows but protect live and incoming state
blocks.explanation: ApplyUpdate sums Text.Length into a long, then repeatedly removes the first list entry that is inactive and is not the changed key until both budgets fit. This is retained-list order, not timestamp sorting or LRU. Active partials and the just-updated/finalized row cannot be sacrificed to make their own update appear successful. If no candidate exists, it throws while the original list and counters remain intact. Only the final assignment publishes the staged list. Whole segments are evicted; text is never truncated.

files.role: Names semantic UI color roles independently of WPF brushes, retaining a distinct solid reading color.

blocks.title: Color roles are data, not a rendering subsystem
blocks.explanation: UiTheme declares DeepSeaFoam, HarborDaylight and Plain. The positional record names Background/Surface/Input fills; Text/Muted/Heading reading hierarchy; Border/Accent/Hover/Selection interaction colors; SelectionText/ActionText foregrounds; Warning/Error statuses; and a separate HighContrastReading foreground. Name is display metadata. The properties are generated init properties on a record, not mutable WPF resources; ThemeBrushes.Apply is the consumer that converts these strings to brushes.

blocks.title: Three complete fixed palettes with rejecting lookup
blocks.explanation: For returns a complete new palette for each supported enum. DeepSeaFoam uses a dark blue-green background and white HighContrastReading; HarborDaylight uses light green/cream surfaces and black reading; Plain uses near-white/gray surfaces and black reading. The ordinary Text colors remain softer and separate from reading white/black. Warning and Error keep dedicated role colors even in Plain. Unsupported enum values throw, avoiding a silent fallback that would hide configuration mistakes. These RGB constants do not encode opacity or establish contrast over a composited desktop.

blocks.title: Toggle companions rather than cycling through every theme
blocks.explanation: NextThemed maps DeepSeaFoam to HarborDaylight and every other input to DeepSeaFoam. Thus Plain exits into the themed pair rather than being the third stop in a cycle. Unlike For, this helper does not reject an invalid enum value; its fallback is part of the actual expression.

files.role: Preserves human-readable transcript/export text with separate source partials and reject-on-overflow behavior instead of structured-history eviction.

blocks.title: Committed text and source-ordered live text are separate
blocks.explanation: A StringBuilder holds committed export history with a 250,000 UTF-16-unit budget, while a dictionary holds current partials by numeric source key. Partial and UnfinishedText omit empty values and sort source keys, so output ordering is deterministic rather than arrival order. UnfinishedText explicitly labels uncertain recognition. Text snapshots the builder as a string; HasContent also checks nonempty partial rendering. The 250,000 cap is not a cap on ExportText including extra live partials and markers.

blocks.title: Preflight session archival before clearing partials
blocks.explanation: BeginSession first refuses a latched full buffer. It prepares unfinished recognition with platform newlines and a session separator whose literal newlines are LF, then checks the entire prospective append before mutation. Overflow sets IsFull and throws while preserving text and partials. Success archives partials, appends a separator only when prior content exists, resets final deduplication and clears the live dictionary. This buffer has no capture GUID; the application and StructuredTranscriptStore enforce session identity.

blocks.title: Partial replacement and final validation precede mutation
blocks.explanation: SetPartial bounds one string at 16,384 UTF-16 units and replaces only the selected source entry. AddFinal resolves a source key, rejects nonpositive IDs, oversized text and nonfinite/negative/over-30-day start offsets, then rejects IDs at/below one global mark before clearing any partial. The optional source supports an unlabeled legacy track. Unlike TranscriptValidation.Text, these methods access value.Length directly rather than providing an explicit null guard.

blocks.title: Format elapsed hours, reject overflow and settle one source
blocks.explanation: The timestamp computes total integer hours separately from TimeSpan's minute/second components, preventing a 25-hour offset from wrapping to hour one. InvariantCulture stabilizes numeric formatting. Empty final text produces no line. Prospective formatted line length includes source label, timestamp and newline; overflow sets IsFull and throws before consuming the ID or removing the partial. Accepted finals advance the ID and clear only their source. Return value means a line was appended, so an accepted empty final returns false, unlike StructuredTranscriptStore.AddFinal.

blocks.title: Explicit export, reset and validated legacy source mapping
blocks.explanation: ExportText returns committed text plus labeled unfinished recognition without modifying either store. Clear removes text/partials, resets the global final mark and releases IsFull. SourceKey maps null to unlabeled zero and the two enum sources to one/two; other numeric values throw InvalidDataException. SourcePrefix converts valid nonzero keys through DisplayName. IsFull is a restart/status latch: SetPartial and AddFinal do not directly test it, so do not describe it as a universal mutation lock.

files.role: Defines immutable structured identity/revision values and centralized validation, keeping display labels separate from provenance.

blocks.title: Identity is the full session/source/epoch/local-ID tuple
blocks.explanation: The key constructor validates a nonempty capture GUID, recognized source, nonnegative epoch and positive local segment ID before assigning getter-only properties. Record value equality includes all four fields; a reused protocol number, identical text or the same microphone cannot identify a segment across sessions/epochs. The key carries no revision because later recognition revises one identity instead of making the user's selection point elsewhere.

blocks.title: Validate text, timing and final/partial consistency
blocks.explanation: A segment is a sealed record with a 16,384-unit text ceiling and 2,592,000-second timing ceiling. Construction requires a key and positive revision, then validates text/timing. Finals must have a positive protocol ID; partials cannot claim any protocol final ID; finals cannot be active partials. A nonfinal inactive segment is legal and represents unfinished historical recognition. Only after all guards pass are the supplied fields assigned unchanged. Optional partial timings are not prohibited, and empty text is valid.

blocks.title: Read-only records, display-only abbreviations and defensive copies
blocks.explanation: All exposed segment fields are getter-only. DisplayText derives its session suffix, source label and Final/Partial/Unfinished partial label from structured fields, then appends literal text; it does not parse embedded labels. The last eight GUID hex digits are only a visual discriminator and are not collision-free identity. Copy constructs another validated segment and clones Key with an empty with-expression. Strings can be shared safely because they are immutable, while callers receive distinct segment/key objects.

blocks.title: Reusable session/source/epoch/text guards
blocks.explanation: TranscriptValidation rejects an empty session GUID with the caller's parameter name, rejects every source except Computer/Microphone, and rejects negative epochs. Text must be nonnull and within the length ceiling, but blank or whitespace text is allowed for recognition settlement. string.Length measures UTF-16 code units and this validator does not reject unpaired surrogates, normalize combining characters or measure encoded bytes; NoteFileStore's strict UTF-8 policy is a different boundary.

blocks.title: Optional timing remains finite, bounded and ordered
blocks.explanation: Timing validates start and end independently, accepting missing values. When both exist, end cannot precede start; equality is allowed. Seconds rejects NaN, either infinity, negative offsets and values above the inclusive 30-day ceiling. These values are seconds rather than wall-clock timestamps or Stopwatch ticks. A missing endpoint is not synthesized from the other.

files.role: Computes finite, work-area-constrained window geometry and the reading-column breakpoint without depending on WPF.

blocks.title: Pure geometry result and named layout constants
blocks.explanation: WorkspaceBounds is a readonly record struct returning position, dimensions and adjusted minima. Defaults request 1240 by 1520, nominal minima are 470 by 560, the two-column threshold is inclusive at 900, and nominal edge inset is 12. UseReadingColumns only compares width and does not validate it. Units are the caller's coordinate space; MainWindow.Layout converts monitor device coordinates into WPF coordinates before calling FitToWorkArea.

blocks.title: Reject invalid work areas and relax minima for small screens
blocks.explanation: FitToWorkArea accepts optional requested size/position but first requires all work-area coordinates/dimensions to be finite and dimensions positive. Its exception always names workWidth, even if another component is invalid. Insets are the smaller of 12 and a quarter of that dimension, leaving usable space even in tiny areas. MinimumWidth/Height are reduced to available space rather than forcing a nominal minimum offscreen. Negative monitor origins are valid.

blocks.title: Normalize requested size before clamping its position
blocks.explanation: Nonfinite requested dimensions fall back to desired dimensions; finite values clamp between adjusted minima and available bounds. Missing/nonfinite coordinates center the already-fitted size, while valid coordinates are preserved as far as possible. Final position clamps use that fitted size, keeping the window inside the inset work area. The function returns values only; native monitor discovery, DPI conversion and applying Width/Height remain the desktop caller's responsibilities.

files.role: Specifies canonical command payloads, rejection boundaries and stable read-only suggestions with synthetic strings rather than application actions.

blocks.title: Compare full command records across canonical and normalized spellings
blocks.explanation: The table specifies kind, optional argument and optional integer for every command family, including record aliases, all enumerated source/theme choices, numeric endpoints and leading-zero font/opacity spellings. Each row compares the complete expected record twice: once from the canonical input and once from uppercased input wrapped in whitespace and one colon. Full-record equality catches misplaced or unexpected payloads, not merely the right enum. These are parser tests only; Start, Ask, Copy and the other names do not execute their corresponding application actions here. Canonical rows also exercise context on/off as full Context records under the same normalization checks.

blocks.title: Distinguish normalization, null failure and an empty suggestion prefix
blocks.explanation: Mixed casing, tabs, CR/LF, em spaces and nonbreaking spaces must parse like canonical commands after removing one leading colon. Null must fail both Parse and Suggest with ArgumentNullException, the authored Enter a built-in command message and parameter text. Empty, whitespace-only and colon-only inputs instead yield Parse's ArgumentException while Suggest returns the first five Examples. The tests preserve the intentional difference between submitting no command and requesting initial suggestions, despite both APIs sharing the tokenizer.

blocks.title: Reject abbreviated names, missing arguments and extra tokens
blocks.explanation: Negative rows exercise unknown verbs, prefixes such as sta, unsupported record/source/clarify/theme subcommands, absent arguments and invalid colon positions. Every one must receive the fixed unknown-command message and parameter text, not a guessed command. A separate loop appends an extra token to every public example and requires failure, tying strict arity to the evolving example list. These assertions prohibit implicit suffix tolerance and shell-like argument interpretation; valid whitespace inside a recognized token sequence remains covered separately. The negative table additionally rejects bare context, context all and context yes, preserving the explicit on/off grammar.

blocks.title: Pin numeric bounds and forbid alternative number notations
blocks.explanation: Font values below eight or above twenty-four and opacity values below ten or above one hundred must report their respective authored range errors. The shared invalid-number matrix then checks fractions, locale commas, scientific notation, NaN/infinities, signs, hexadecimal, separators, suffixes, Int32 overflow and non-ASCII digit forms against both commands. The errors must identify parameter text without confusing the two ranges. Accepted endpoints and leading zeroes appear in the earlier positive table; rejection is not evidence of a blanket ban on every noncanonical decimal spelling.

blocks.title: Restore both cultures after testing invariant parsing
blocks.explanation: For Turkish, French and Saudi Arabic cultures, the fixture changes both CurrentCulture and CurrentUICulture, parses uppercase words and ordinary decimal values, and checks normalized clarify suggestions. A comma decimal still fails. The finally block restores both original cultures even if an assertion throws, avoiding contamination of subsequent work. These cases exercise culture independence of the chosen word and number paths; they do not simulate keyboard layouts, IME composition or translated UI labels.

blocks.title: Count raw UTF-16 input before trimming or limiting suggestions
blocks.explanation: A help command padded to exactly 128 units must parse and suggest successfully, while adding one space must make both APIs throw the length error. The next fixture includes the leading colon in that same budget. Sixty-five supplementary emoji occupy 130 UTF-16 code units and must fail Parse and Suggest even with maximum zero. Together these controls catch moving the check after trimming, after colon removal, or behind an empty-result shortcut; they do not measure bytes or user-perceived glyph count.

blocks.title: Do not trim away forbidden control characters
blocks.explanation: The control-character table includes NUL, backspace, vertical tab, form feed, escape, DEL and selected C1 controls. Each is placed before help, after help and between source and mic; both Parse and Suggest must reject all three positions with the authored control-character message. Edge positions specifically guard against trimming before validation, while the middle position guards against treating every control as a legal separator. Tab, CR and LF are deliberately absent because the earlier positive normalization cases allow them.

blocks.title: Treat shell-shaped and instruction-shaped text as invalid data
blocks.explanation: The matrix supplies chaining operators, newlines joining separate commands, substitutions, quoted values, comments, redirection, executable-looking text and an instruction-like sentence. Parse must throw ArgumentException without embedding the complete supplied input in its message, retain parameter text, and Suggest must return no matches. This validates the deterministic allowlist and the error non-echo behavior for these samples. It is not a shell sandbox or model-safety trial: the tests neither start processes nor send text to a provider.

blocks.title: Keep the public examples canonical, complete by family and read-only
blocks.explanation: Examples must be nonempty, unique under ordinal case-insensitive comparison, trimmed, lowercase and colon-free. Parsing them must cover exactly the enum's command families; explicit font 14 and opacity 55 assertions preserve representative numeric entries. Further tests snapshot Examples and suggestions for matching, unmatched and empty prefixes, exercise the shared mutation-rejection helper, and compare later reads with the snapshots. These checks protect collection exposure, including empty results, without claiming that Examples enumerates every valid numeric command.

blocks.title: Preserve prefix ordering, clamp counts and distinguish no match from invalid syntax
blocks.explanation: Source suggestions must retain mic/computer/both declaration order across casing, whitespace and colon normalization; partial source M, record, font and copy prefixes have exact expected results. Maximum values from Int32.MinValue through Int32.MaxValue must clamp to 0..20, with the omitted limit still five. A larger maximum never pads the three theme matches. Unknown prefixes and invalid commands may have no suggestions, but so does valid font 8 because it is not a curated example. Empty suggestions therefore cannot substitute for Parse or disable otherwise valid submission.

blocks.title: Verify snapshot lifetime and reject mutable collection backdoors
blocks.explanation: A saved copy-suggestion result must survive later suggestion and parse calls unchanged. Separate assertions pin the public 128-input and 8..24-font constants without exercising a real slider. AssertReadOnly rejects a raw string array, casts to generic IList, checks IsReadOnly and requires Add/Clear to throw; nonempty lists must also reject replacement and RemoveAt. It repeats read-only, Add and Clear checks through nongeneric IList. The helper tests actual mutation attempts rather than trusting only the IReadOnlyList static type, which by itself would not prevent a mutable underlying collection.

files.role: Exercises allowed key resolution, strict settings schema and bounded read-only file loading using disposable synthetic files, not global hotkey registration.

blocks.title: Isolate filesystem fixtures and pin the default key and path
blocks.explanation: Each test instance creates a GUID-named .keyboard-shortcut-tests directory relative to the working directory and uses its keyboard.json, rather than writing the user's default settings. ValidKeys enumerates all twenty-five ASCII letters except E and the eleven function keys F1-F11 with exact expected virtual-key values. The default test validates a new record, requires Enabled=true, K and 0x4B, and compares the configured default path with LocalApplicationData/PhantomFudge/keyboard.json. That path assertion does not open the real settings file or register any shortcut.

blocks.title: Round-trip every allowed key in both cases and enabled states
blocks.explanation: For each ValidKeys row, nested loops test the original and lowercase spellings with Enabled both true and false. The constructed record must validate and resolve the exact virtual key while retaining its supplied ActivationKey casing. WriteSettings serializes the synthetic configuration, Load must return a value-equal record, and the loaded record must resolve the same virtual key. This connects direct key validation to file loading and prevents Disabled from becoming an alternate validation path. It proves data mapping only, not OS acceptance of those keys.

blocks.title: Reject unsupported keys even when activation is disabled
blocks.explanation: Negative inputs explicitly include F12 and f12, alongside E/e, blank or padded names, multi-letter names, digits, other out-of-range or zero-prefixed function keys, signed/fractional/exponential function syntax, Unicode lookalikes, control characters and command-shaped strings. For both enabled states, Validate must throw the authored F1-F11 ArgumentException naming ActivationKey, VirtualKey must also throw, and loading the serialized value must fail rather than default. A separate null-key test checks direct record validation and property access; JSON null is a different schema-kind failure covered later. No settings are normalized into an accepted alternative.

blocks.title: Separate absent settings from explicit and configured path selection
blocks.explanation: Missing-file and missing-directory tests require default records without creating the missing filesystem objects. Two fixtures temporarily replace the mutable FilePath and restore it in finally: omitted and null arguments must use that path, while an explicit file must load successfully even when the configured default contains invalid JSON. The latter makes accidental default-path access observable. All writes remain in the instance fixture directory; these tests neither rewrite the user's configuration nor establish a synchronized policy for concurrent mutation of FilePath.

blocks.title: Reject structural schema errors without repairing the file
blocks.explanation: The schema matrix includes non-object roots, missing fields, unsupported or non-Int32 version representations, wrong enabled/key value kinds, unknown options and mis-cased property names. Each valid-JSON input must raise InvalidDataException and retain exact string equality with File.ReadAllText afterward; this is a text comparison, not a byte-array comparison. It guards against silent defaulting or automatic rewriting on schema rejection. In particular, schemaVersion 1.0 and 1e0 are deliberately rejected rather than treated as the accepted integer spelling; malformed JSON and unsupported string key values have their own exception tests.

blocks.title: Compare decoded names and preserve distinct JSON parse failures
blocks.explanation: Repeated schemaVersion, enabled or activationKey must report the duplicate-property InvalidDataException, including a literal enabled name paired with an escaped spelling of the same decoded name. Empty/incomplete text, comments, trailing commas, multiple roots and single-quoted syntax must instead propagate a JsonException subtype. A positive object reorders properties, adds whitespace and uses escaped key/name characters; it still loads disabled lowercase k. These controls distinguish strict JSON syntax and decoded-name identity from raw-text equality or a blanket ban on escape sequences.

blocks.title: Accept a leading UTF-8 BOM without tolerating malformed bytes
blocks.explanation: The BOM fixture explicitly concatenates UTF-8 preamble bytes with a valid settings object, loads default-valued settings and compares the complete stored byte array afterward. The invalid-encoding fixture inserts byte FF inside the key string and requires the authored UTF-8 InvalidDataException, not replacement-character decoding or an unrelated unsupported-key failure. These tests establish acceptance and nonmutation for the BOM case and rejection for this malformed byte sequence; they are not an exhaustive decoder conformance suite.

blocks.title: Exercise inclusive byte limits before key or JSON interpretation
blocks.explanation: Valid ASCII JSON padded to exactly 1,024 bytes must load; one appended space must trigger the size message. A second control pads to 1,021 bytes before adding the three-byte BOM and likewise rejects the next byte. Replacing K with 510 accented characters creates JSON shorter than 1,024 characters but longer than 1,024 UTF-8 bytes, and must fail with the size error before key validation. A 64 KiB file must also be rejected. These assertions test limit behavior; the bounded 1,025-byte read allocation is established by loader source, not measured memory usage here.

blocks.title: Do not disguise access errors or stale configuration as defaults
blocks.explanation: An empty path must throw ArgumentException, an existing directory must throw UnauthorizedAccessException in this filesystem environment, and a file held with FileShare.None must cause IOException. None is treated like a missing settings file. Sequential rewrites then change F1/enabled to F11/disabled: a new Load must observe the new content while the previously returned record remains unchanged. Replacing the file with an invalid empty object must fail rather than returning either cached valid value. These are sequential I/O controls, not a concurrent writer or atomic-snapshot test.

blocks.title: Restore culture and remove only the owned fixture directory
blocks.explanation: Turkish and Saudi Arabic culture rows write lowercase i and f11 and require invariant virtual keys 0x49 and 0x7A. CurrentCulture is restored in finally even on failure. WriteSettings consistently emits exactly schemaVersion=1, enabled and activationKey through JsonSerializer; IDisposable cleanup recursively deletes the instance's GUID-named directory. The fixtures exercise local parsing and synthetic filesystem state, not RegisterHotKey, application focus, microphone capture, model calls or real keyboard input. Source assertions do not by themselves establish that a test run passed.

files.role: Exercises synthetic JSONL flushing, rotation, observable I/O failure and selected metadata rejection controls without live content.

blocks.title: Dispose drains one metadata record with no Text field
blocks.explanation: A unique temporary directory isolates the logger. The test enqueues a synthetic AnswerStarted record, leaves the using scope to drain it, reads exactly one line/file, parses JSON and checks enum spelling, Count=42 and absence of Text. The finally block deletes the fixture. This checks null omission and a simple successful drain, not that the raw sink rejects supplied text or that all shutdowns meet the timeout.

blocks.title: Rotation controls with a queue deliberately larger than the workload
blocks.explanation: The test configures 1,024-byte files, three retained files and 200 queue slots, then submits 100 small metadata records, requiring every enqueue to succeed. After disposal, it checks one to three files and every length within 1..1,024 bytes, then cleans up. Despite the method name, no individually oversized record is submitted: this proves ordinary-record file-size rotation, not record_limit handling, channel saturation, exact retained content or competing writers.

blocks.title: A file at the directory path is a deliberate I/O obstacle
blocks.explanation: The fixture writes a harmless ordinary file where a directory is expected, enqueues ApplicationStarted and disposes to wait for processing. It asserts diagnostic_io and exactly one dropped record, while cleanup removes the obstacle. The using declaration causes a second disposal at scope exit, exercising idempotence incidentally. It does not construct application state despite the test name, and does not test directory links, permission recovery or a timed-out flush.

blocks.title: Negative controls run before the static sink is touched
blocks.explanation: A code containing spaces, an unrecognized provider string and a negative audio count each must throw ArgumentException through LocalDiagnostics.Record. IncludeText must remain false in this test context. These deliberately rejected calls need not create a real static log. They do not prove semantic redaction of an allowed token, validate diagnostics.json parsing, exercise content opt-in/truncation or inspect sanitized exception frames.

files.role: Specifies strict UTF-8/BOM fidelity, optimistic conflict behavior and preservation of prior files under bounded synthetic failures.

blocks.title: Isolated directory and byte-sensitive round-trip fixtures
blocks.explanation: Each test instance creates a GUID-named temporary directory and deletes it recursively on disposal. The two BOM cases write a synthetic string containing CRLF, LF, accented text, a surrogate-pair emoji and a combining sequence. Readback must preserve exact text/BOM and match the writer's fingerprint. A single remaining file checks that a successful path leaves no temporary. It does not simulate an external writer during the read.

blocks.title: Creation refusal, changed-file refusal and matching-hash replacement
blocks.explanation: Three controls distinguish modes: an existing file plus null expected fingerprint must retain existing text; an external rewrite after the initial snapshot must retain external text and leave only one file; a matching fingerprint must permit replacement and produce a different fingerprint. These checks exercise before/after operations sequentially. They establish observed-conflict behavior, not an atomic lock against changes in the final verification-to-move gap.

blocks.title: Deletion, malformed bytes and oversized opens are not normalized away
blocks.explanation: Deleting a previously saved file must make replacement with its old fingerprint fail, and the path must remain absent rather than silently recreated. Bytes FF FE FF deliberately fail strict UTF-8 decoding. A MaximumBytes+1 file must raise InvalidDataException during read. These are distinct failure classes; the tests do not assume every read failure is a NoteConflictException or a recoverable encoding conversion.

blocks.title: Save preflight preserves original and counts encoded bytes
blocks.explanation: An oversized ASCII save must throw while original content and the one-file directory remain intact. Fits separately accepts exactly 1 MiB of ASCII without BOM, rejects the same text with three BOM bytes, rejects 1 MiB characters of two-byte accented text and rejects an unpaired high surrogate. This is the negative control against confusing UTF-16 string length with UTF-8 storage length; it is not a complete Unicode normalization or all-boundary test matrix.

blocks.title: Already-cancelled replacement leaves the old file
blocks.explanation: The test creates an original snapshot, cancels a CancellationTokenSource before WriteAsync, expects an OperationCanceledException subtype, and verifies original bytes and no temporary leftovers. Cancellation is arranged before the call rather than injected between temporary flush and rename; the test does not prove every possible cancellation race or power-loss outcome.

files.role: Declares the .NET 10 xUnit test assembly, its Core dependency and directly linked non-UI launcher helpers.

blocks.title: Test host, assertion namespace and isolated launcher source links
blocks.explanation: The nonpackable net10.0 project enables nullable/implicit usings and references the pinned test SDK, xUnit and runner. Using supplies the global Xunit namespace; ProjectReference compiles against Core. Six Compile links include actual non-UI launcher source for contract, process handoff, token and maintenance tests without depending on its WPF entry point. They are not duplicate implementations or permission to run a real service. Directory.Build.props contributes shared correctness settings. Declarations alone do not establish passing execution.

files.role: Defines explicit selection, exact composition, edit ownership, atomic rejection and refresh isolation through synthetic transcript mutations.

blocks.title: An available transcript is not implicit question permission
blocks.explanation: Two fixed GUIDs define independent synthetic sessions. The first test populates a store with a final, creates a draft and calls Refresh without selecting anything. It requires a nonempty question ID but revision zero, empty text/selection, false flags and Freeze rejection. This is a negative control for hidden whole-transcript import, not a UI click or network test.

blocks.title: Caller order and first occurrence beat transcript order or newest revision
blocks.explanation: The first selection is deliberately third/first/third/second/first; expected text and keys are third/first/second with one revision and distinct copied segment/key objects. A second test supplies two versions of the same partial key and requires the first chosen text/revision, not the newer hidden alternative. Together these reject sorting, duplicate concatenation and latest-revision substitution inside ReplaceSelection.

blocks.title: Only explicitly selected inputs contribute literal text
blocks.explanation: A store contains remote context, unrelated prior microphone text and a selected microphone partial. Selecting the partial alone must exclude both others; explicitly adding remote context includes it in the supplied order but still excludes unrelated microphone text. Another fixture embeds a Computer label in microphone text, whitespace/newlines and a decomposed accent. Composition and Freeze preserve the string exactly while provenance remains Microphone, disproving label parsing and normalization.

blocks.title: No-op replacement and defensive collection copies
blocks.explanation: Repeating the same segment twice must preserve revision one, selection object identity and QuestionId. The next test replaces the input array entry after selection, checks copied segment/key objects with equal values, attempts IList.Add/index replacement and expects NotSupportedException, then clears the draft while retaining the old collection snapshot. These controls test both caller-array aliasing and read-only collection mutation, not merely property setter absence.

blocks.title: Refresh follows one selected key from partial to final
blocks.explanation: The test selects a microphone partial, introduces an unselected Computer partial, revises the microphone and checks both draft and source revision two with the same key. Repeating Refresh is a no-op. Final ID nine then yields revision three, final metadata and no provisional flag while keeping QuestionId. A new microphone utterance must not join the draft. This is explicit evidence against source-wide or latest-utterance retargeting.

blocks.title: Refresh preserves selection order and cannot overwrite a correction
blocks.explanation: One test selects Mic before Computer although store order is reversed, finalizes both and requires Mic-first composition. The next edits a selected partial to a whitespace-sensitive correction, sends a different ASR final and requires exact corrected text, unchanged selected collection/revision and original ASR provenance still provisional. User editing freezes provenance refresh as well as visible text; it does not rewrite the original partial into a final.

blocks.title: Edit intent is independent of changed characters and can be reset explicitly
blocks.explanation: Reasserting identical text sets UserEdited without increasing revision; later different partial text must not enter the draft. A separate test selects ASR, edits to corrected text, then explicitly replaces from the store: UserEdited becomes false, ASR text returns and a subsequent ASR update is accepted at draft revision four. These paired controls define the policy switch and its authorized reversal rather than assuming every EditText increments revision.

blocks.title: Typed questions stay source-free and empty replacement is not Clear
blocks.explanation: A typed-only exact string must survive Refresh despite available unselected ASR and freeze with no source refs or provisional status. Empty ReplaceSelection explicitly removes typed/selected state, resets edit/provisional flags and increments revision while retaining the same QuestionId; repeating it is a no-op. The fixture text says bytes, but the assertion compares .NET strings, not a serialized byte payload.

blocks.title: Empty finals remove guesses and empty records add no separators
blocks.explanation: A selected guess receives an empty final: text must become empty, the same key remains with final status, Freeze must fail and a later utterance must not resurrect it. The next test selects five finals with only two nonempty texts, requiring exactly one platform separator while retaining all five provenance records. This distinguishes text composition from provenance count and prevents an empty final being treated as no update.

blocks.title: Session closure and eviction do not fabricate or retarget selections
blocks.explanation: After a session change, a selected unfinished partial refreshes to inactive but remains provisional, keeps the original session/key and has no protocol final ID; unrelated new-session final text is excluded. A second test selects an old final in a one-slot store, evicts it, clears/restarts the store and requires the same selection object/text/revision and old-session provenance at Freeze. These cases show copied selection independence from current store membership.

blocks.title: Missing unfinished copies persist and mixed sessions fail atomically
blocks.explanation: An old partial is closed and evicted before Refresh in a one-slot store; the selected copy remains the same object and provisional, not retargeted to a new-session partial. Because it cannot refresh from a missing key, its historical IsActive flag is not asserted as current truth. A cross-session replacement then deliberately follows an edited draft and must fail with parameter segments while preserving text, collection identity, revision, QuestionId and UserEdited.

blocks.title: Nulls and a throwing iterator cannot partially publish a selection
blocks.explanation: Null enumerable, an enumerable containing a valid item then null, and null Refresh store are checked with parameter-name assertions. A separate FailingSelection iterator yields one otherwise valid new segment and then throws; old text, selected collection identity and revision must remain intact. This tests staging across enumeration itself, not just prevalidating a materialized list.

blocks.title: Single and joined selection limits preserve the prior state
blocks.explanation: A selected string of 8,193 units is legal as transcript text but too large for a question; rejection must preserve an edited draft and its flags/revision, with segments and 8192 in the diagnostic. The next case constructs two strings that total exactly 8,192 including Environment.NewLine.Length, accepts and freezes them, then adds one more segment and requires atomic rejection. This is the negative control for omitting separator cost from the budget.

blocks.title: Edit rejection and oversized final refresh retain an inspectable draft
blocks.explanation: Null and 8,193-unit EditText calls must leave the unedited selected draft intact; exactly 8,192 units are accepted and frozen. Separately, an oversized final is accepted into the transcript store but Refresh must throw InvalidOperationException with a retained-state message, leaving the short selected partial, ID/revision and provisional flag. Freeze still captures that old short text. An explicit shorter edit then blocks further refresh, demonstrating recovery without truncation or hidden provenance replacement.

blocks.title: A rejected long partial can recover on a newer shorter revision
blocks.explanation: The draft combines a 4,000-unit final and a short partial; expanding the partial to 4,200 exceeds the question budget once joined, so Refresh must retain old text, collection identity and revision one. A later shorter partial succeeds, advances the draft only to revision two, and carries source revision three. This separates skipped source revisions from successfully published draft revisions.

blocks.title: Empty provenance is count-bounded and Unicode whitespace cannot freeze
blocks.explanation: Selecting 256 unique empty finals is allowed but a 257th must fail without changing the selected collection/revision. Concatenating duplicate copies of those same 256 remains a no-op because deduplication precedes count enforcement. Blank, ASCII whitespace and em-space/nonbreaking-space drafts are valid editable strings but Freeze rejects them. This distinguishes selection cardinality from composed text length and blank-question policy from text storage validation.

blocks.title: Clear prevents late refresh resurrection and helpers keep fixtures synthetic
blocks.explanation: After selection/edit, Clear must create a different nonempty question GUID, reset revision and all state, and prevent a late final from repopulating the draft. A second Clear must create another identity. FailingSelection is the real iterator negative control: it yields uncommitted content then throws. Final builds valid microphone finals with matching synthetic protocol IDs; Started creates an explicit session with optional capacity. These helpers involve no devices, model or network and do not prove concurrent caller safety.

files.role: Verifies exact frozen text, bounded monotonic creation timing, copied provenance and independence from every later local mutation in the fixtures.

blocks.title: Freeze samples one revision without normalizing text
blocks.explanation: Fixed GUIDs support later fixtures. This test types tabs, a combining accent, a snowman, CRLF and trailing spaces, brackets Freeze with Stopwatch.GetTimestamp and requires exact ID/revision/text plus creation time within that interval. Typed-only SourceRefs are empty, WasProvisional false and UserEdited true. Revision remains one. It tests monotonic-clock sampling, not UTC conversion or uniqueness of successive tick values.

blocks.title: A saved snapshot survives an aggressive mutation chain
blocks.explanation: The fixture freezes a selected partial, then revises/finalizes ASR, evicts it with another source in a one-slot store, edits/clears the draft, clears/restarts the store and selects a new-session partial. Assertions require the original exact text, question identity, revision, timestamp and provisional/edit flags to remain unchanged, with the original session/epoch/source revision and no final ID. This sequential stress chain tests aliasing isolation; it does not test unsynchronized threads.

blocks.title: Deep copying includes keys and all final provenance
blocks.explanation: An epoch-three partial becomes protocol final 27 with fractional start/end times. After selection and Freeze, the snapshot record must be value-equal to the store record but not the same object as either store or draft record, and its key must also be distinct. Revision, protocol ID, epoch and timing are checked explicitly. IList replacement, Clear and Add must throw. These controls test list and nested-record boundaries rather than only comparing text.

blocks.title: Corrected payload and original ASR provenance intentionally differ
blocks.explanation: The user corrects a selected partial before a late ASR final. Refresh is blocked by edit ownership, and Freeze must contain corrected ExactText at draft revision two while SourceRefs retain uncorrected source revision one without protocol metadata. WasProvisional stays true because it describes selected provenance, not whether corrected prose is usable. This is the negative control against serializing SourceRefs as though they were the intended question.

blocks.title: Repeated Freeze is not another edit or another question identity
blocks.explanation: Two freezes of the first typed revision must be distinct objects sharing QuestionId and SnapshotRevision while leaving the draft at revision one. Editing to second text increments revision for the next snapshot without changing the prior one. Clear followed by another edit creates a different QuestionId and starts revision one again. The test does not assert strict timestamp increase or record equality between repeated snapshots.

blocks.title: Cross-source snapshots exclude unselected history
blocks.explanation: The store contains unrelated microphone text, explicit Computer context and a new microphone question. Selection deliberately chooses question then context; Freeze must keep that text/source order, exactly two refs, provisional status and no edit flag. An explicit DoesNotContain assertion guards against adding the unrelated earlier microphone final. Available same-source history is not implicit authorization.

files.role: Checks source-aware human-readable transcript behavior separately from structured selection identity.

blocks.title: Finalize one track and preserve both unfinished tracks on restart
blocks.explanation: Computer and Mic partials are set together. Finalizing Computer must append its timestamp/source label, remove only its old partial and preserve Mic; finalizing Mic removes the rest, with 0.5 seconds rendered as second zero. A restart fixture archives both unfinished tracks with explicit labels, empties the live view and accepts a new final ID one. These are formatter/state tests, not proof of actual simultaneous capture.

blocks.title: Empty finals and duplicate IDs must not erase another input
blocks.explanation: An empty microphone final returns false for no appended line yet clears only Mic, leaving Computer and no committed text. In the second control, a Computer final consumes ID one, and a duplicate Mic final with that same global ID must neither append replayed text nor clear the pending Mic partial. The assertions distinguish accepted empty settlement from rejected duplicate behavior despite both returning false.

blocks.title: Clear, invalid source rejection and literal input labels
blocks.explanation: Clear removes both tracks and committed text, resets HasContent and allows ID one again. Numeric source 99 must fail in partial/final buffer APIs and WireName. The two data rows pin computer/Computer and microphone/Mic wire/display mappings. Labels represent inputs, not speakers; these tests neither infer diarization nor check a device permission UI. DisplayName's invalid default exists in source but is not separately asserted here.

files.role: Checks immutable public model shape, full key equality and explicit rejection of inconsistent identity, metadata and timing.

blocks.title: Change one key field at a time and inspect setter absence
blocks.explanation: The equality test holds three identity fields constant while changing session, source, epoch or local ID in turn, and requires each to produce an unequal key. Reflection then requires no SetMethod on public properties of TranscriptSegmentKey, TranscriptSegment and QuestionSnapshot. This catches accidental public/init setters on those types, but does not by itself prove nested collection immutability; separate draft/snapshot tests exercise that.

blocks.title: Constructor guards expose precise invalid parameters
blocks.explanation: Invalid key cases use empty GUID, numeric source zero, epoch -1 and local ID zero. Invalid segment cases use null key, revision zero, null text and 16,385-unit text. Each checks both exception type and parameter name, showing constructor validation before an invalid value object can escape. No UTF-8 encoding or grapheme validity is tested by these string-length controls.

blocks.title: Finality cannot be inferred without valid final metadata
blocks.explanation: The theory supplies null, zero and negative protocol IDs to a final and requires protocolSegmentId errors. A separate negative control rejects a partial that claims final ID one and a final that also claims isActive=true. These cases preserve the distinction between active provisional, closed unfinished and final states; they do not require every inactive segment to be final.

blocks.title: Rendered source/finality labels cannot override structured fields
blocks.explanation: Literal text containing Computer and Final labels is put in an active microphone partial; expected DisplayText prepends the real Mic/Partial fields and keeps the misleading text literal. A second fixture uses equal text/source in two sessions and checks the eight-digit session suffix and unfinished/partial/final labels. Distinct chosen suffixes demonstrate display discrimination for these fixtures, not global uniqueness of an abbreviated GUID.

blocks.title: Direct construction also rejects bad timing
blocks.explanation: Creating finals directly, without StructuredTranscriptStore, must reject NaN start, positive-infinity end and reversed finite timing. This ensures validation is a model invariant rather than only an ingestion guard. The broader optional-boundary matrix lives in StructuredTranscriptStoreTests; this test does not assert every numeric edge.

files.role: Exercises session/epoch identity, staged partial/final updates, protected eviction, bounded duplicate handling and precise invalid-input rejection.

blocks.title: Explicit start and positive capacity preconditions
blocks.explanation: Synthetic fixed GUIDs identify two sessions. An unstarted store must remain empty and return false for valid partial/final events from a nonempty session, rather than implicitly adopting it. Four capacity rows reject zero/negative segment or character budgets with the exact parameter name. These cases distinguish absent active session from malformed event input.

blocks.title: Stable local identity survives revised text and real protocol IDs
blocks.explanation: A first partial is active/nonfinal at revision one without protocol metadata; identical text is accepted unchanged. Revised text creates revision two while the old record retains its original string. Final protocol ID 72 keeps the local key, adds timing and revision three, and is explicitly unequal to the local ID. A later partial has a new key/revision one. A final-only fixture uses protocol ID 200 but local ID one, proving the two numbering systems are independent.

blocks.title: Cross-source partial isolation and session-global duplicate rejection
blocks.explanation: Finalizing Computer must leave Mic's record active and equal to its prior value. A second test establishes final ID ten, then sends Mic duplicate ten with a higher epoch and older nine with empty text. Both must return false without changing the snapshot or poisoning epoch zero; real final eleven is then accepted. This is a targeted negative control for applying source/epoch state before the global duplicate guard.

blocks.title: New sessions close partials, reject old callbacks and reject retained GUID reuse
blocks.explanation: Session restart retains an old final and converts the old partial to inactive unfinished with same key/text, revision+1 and no protocol final ID. Old-session partial/final callbacks return false, while the new session accepts final ID one with a new local ID and display suffix. Invalid empty/current/retained session starts throw without altering the existing state. The reuse test only covers IDs still current or retained, not a durable all-history GUID registry.

blocks.title: Clear invalidates callbacks; epoch change affects only its own source
blocks.explanation: Clear must empty the store and current GUID, reject old callbacks and preserve an earlier array snapshot; restarting cannot reuse the old local ID. The epoch test starts both inputs, advances Mic to epoch one, keeps Computer equal, closes old Mic without finality and allocates a different Mic key. Old-epoch partial/final callbacks return false without consuming final ID 50; epoch-one final ID one and Computer epoch-zero updates still work.

blocks.title: New-epoch finals are new utterances, while empty partials reuse existing keys
blocks.explanation: An epoch-two final arriving after an epoch-zero guess must leave that old guess inactive/nonfinal and create a new final in epoch two.
