The next test accepts an empty partial on an empty track without adding a row, then creates a guess, changes it to empty and revises again; the existing key survives and revisions advance two then three. Empty input is therefore neither always ignored nor always a new segment.

blocks.title: Empty final settlement and a ten-thousand-event deduplication flood
blocks.explanation: An empty Mic final must leave Computer untouched, settle the same Mic key to empty/final/inactive, and not create a new entry on the next empty final. A flood alternates sources across 10,000 increasing empty final IDs in a two-slot/ten-unit store; no rows should exist, yet replayed ID one and duplicate ID 10,000 must be rejected. The test observes bounded segment state, not a heap profiler, while source code explains the constant-size high-water mark.

blocks.title: Evict complete historical rows instead of trimming incoming text
blocks.explanation: A two-row store accepts three finals and must retain second/third; replaying the evicted first protocol ID still fails. A six-character store accepts aaa and bbb, then cccc, requiring both prior rows to disappear and the incoming string to remain whole. These controls independently exercise count and text budgets, retention order and deduplication independent of retained content.

blocks.title: Protect live keys from remote churn and growing text
blocks.explanation: A live selected Mic partial is held while 100 Computer finals churn through a two-slot store. Its key must stay first and survive later revision/finalization with global final 101. A separate eight-character budget lets a growing Mic partial evict an old Computer final but not change the partial key. These tests show why live rows are ineligible victims; they do not mean closed unfinished history is permanently pinned.

blocks.title: Capacity failure cannot consume epochs, keys or final IDs
blocks.explanation: With two live partials near the text budget, a growth failure and an oversized new-epoch final must leave the prior records unchanged; the same final ID eight then succeeds in old epoch zero. A one-slot store rejects both another live partial and an incoming final without discarding Mic; an empty Computer update and Mic final ID one still succeed. Finally, a single too-large incoming row cannot evict history and commit a truncated result: failure preserves old state and the same final ID can later carry fitting text.

blocks.title: Closed partial eviction and read-only array snapshot lifetime
blocks.explanation: In a one-slot store, starting a new session closes the old guess and allows a new partial to evict it; callbacks from the old session remain rejected. Another fixture casts Segments to IList, requires read-only mutation failures, then revises/clears the store while the previously captured snapshot still shows original text and revision one. This verifies array membership isolation and immutable records without requiring a deep clone on every Segments getter.

blocks.title: Check both budgets after every event and reject unknown sources
blocks.explanation: A fixed live Mic key coexists with 500 Computer finals whose text lengths cycle through zero to nineteen. After each event the test asserts 1..7 segments, 0..80 text units and the same live key, catching intermediate bound violations rather than checking only the final state. Numeric sources zero, three and 255 must fail both ingestion methods with source parameter errors and leave the store empty. This is deterministic single-caller testing, not a concurrent load benchmark.

blocks.title: Reject null/oversized input but retain maximum exact text
blocks.explanation: After arranging a keep partial, null and 16,385-unit text failures on both APIs must preserve the prior snapshot, and final ID one remains available. Another test builds exactly 16,384 units with leading space/tab and trailing CRLF, accepts it as partial and as int.MaxValue final, and requires exact equality. These assertions rule out trimming/truncation and ID consumption on rejected input; they do not validate every Unicode scalar sequence.

blocks.title: Empty session, negative epoch and invalid final IDs are errors, not stale events
blocks.explanation: Both ingestion methods must identify an empty session parameter and negative sourceEpoch precisely, leaving no rows. Final IDs zero, -1 and int.MinValue separately require segmentId errors. These tests specify argument validation before current-session/duplicate handling: malformed data is not quietly categorized as an obsolete callback.

blocks.title: Bad timing preserves state and does not burn a final ID
blocks.explanation: NaN, both infinities, -0.1 and 2,592,001 are each tested independently as start and end, checking exact parameter names and preservation of a keep partial. Reversed finite timing must name endSeconds, after which the same final ID one succeeds with start zero/end MaximumSeconds. The retry is the negative control against consuming identity before validating timing.

blocks.title: Optional and inclusive timing bounds plus explicit-session helper
blocks.explanation: The matrix accepts both endpoints absent, only one endpoint present, zero-duration at zero and zero-duration at the 30-day maximum, retaining exact nullable values. It also accepts long.MaxValue as source epoch; epochs are identifiers, not durations. Started constructs a store with supplied budgets and calls BeginSession with the fixed GUID, ensuring every other fixture that uses it has an explicit start. This matrix is source-read evidence of intended assertions, not a claim that tests were run here.

files.role: Pins palette role constants, toggle policy and mathematical contrast checks for opaque RGB pairs.

blocks.title: Canonical role values, companion toggling and invalid palette rejection
blocks.explanation: Three data rows pin Background, Surface, Text and Accent for every theme. Toggle assertions require the two themed palettes to alternate and Plain to exit to DeepSeaFoam. For((UiTheme)99) must throw rather than silently select Plain. These tests pin only the listed four canonical roles here, not every palette field, and do not test invalid NextThemed input.

blocks.title: Ordinary and high-contrast reading roles have different assertions
blocks.explanation: Every theme must achieve computed contrast at least 4.5 for Text/Background, SelectionText/Selection and ActionText/Accent. HighContrastReading must be exact white for dark or black for light/plain, distinct from ordinary Text and a three-byte RGB color. It must reach at least 12 against Background/Surface/Input and seven against Selection. These are opaque color-pair assertions, not rendered WPF accessibility approval or contrast guarantees over arbitrary translucent backdrops.

blocks.title: Compute contrast using linearized sRGB luminance
blocks.explanation: The helper parses hex RGB, scales channels to 0..1, linearizes values using the 0.04045 threshold with either division by 12.92 or the 2.4-power curve, then weights RGB by 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722. Contrast is (lighter+0.05)/(darker+0.05). There is no alpha blending, font-size/rendering model or desktop-background sampling, explaining the deliberately opaque scope of the tests.

files.role: Tests export-oriented replacement, restart preservation, formatting and reject-on-capacity behavior using unlabeled synthetic input.

blocks.title: Partial replacement, unfinished export and duplicate final controls
blocks.explanation: Setting a then a sentence must replace the current partial without appending committed text, while ExportText labels it unfinished. A final hello at second two clears the partial and appends exactly one timestamped line. Repeating ID one with both identical text and deliberately different replayed data returns false, guarding against deduplication based only on string equality.

blocks.title: Restart retains history and refuses an oversized archival append
blocks.explanation: Restart after a final keeps old text and a session separator while permitting final ID one again. Restart with an unfinished partial archives it explicitly rather than finalizing or dropping it. The capacity control fills fifteen 16,000-unit finals, adds another 16,000-unit partial, captures ExportText, then expects BeginSession failure with identical export text and retained content. It exercises preflight ordering before partial clear, not automatic persistence to disk.

blocks.title: Reject invalid offsets/IDs and preserve total elapsed hours
blocks.explanation: Offset rows cover negative one, NaN, positive infinity and one second beyond the 30-day ceiling; ID rows reject zero and negative one. Each expects InvalidDataException. A positive control at 90,001 seconds must start with 25:00:01, exposing a formatter that incorrectly used a TimeSpan hour component modulo 24. This is text-format validation, not clock synchronization.

blocks.title: Overflow rejects incoming history and latches restart until clear
blocks.explanation: After fifteen 16,000-unit finals, the next final must throw, set IsFull and leave all prior committed text unchanged. BeginSession must also refuse while full. Clear resets full/content state and makes restart legal again. The final test rejects a 16,385-unit partial. These assertions verify this path's preservation; they do not claim IsFull blocks every subsequent SetPartial/AddFinal call or that ExportText including partials is capped at 250,000.

files.role: Pins desired geometry, work-area containment, recovery positions and the responsive reading threshold with pure numeric fixtures.

blocks.title: Large desired size with bounded minima across monitor geometries
blocks.explanation: The first test pins the desired dimensions to twice 620 by 760, expects full desired size in a large work area and retains nominal minima. Five area rows include ordinary monitors, negative origins and a screen smaller than nominal minima. Assertions require position containment, dimensions at least the returned minima and no larger than work area or desired size. These are pure geometry cases, not real monitor/DPI or native-window tests.

blocks.title: Preserve valid user placement, recover offscreen and pin the breakpoint
blocks.explanation: A valid 720-by-620 window at 100,150 must remain unchanged. An offscreen 600-by-600 window requested at 9000,-1000 on a negative-origin monitor is moved to -612,12 without enlarging it, testing both inset edges. Width rows 470/899 are stacked and 900/1240 use columns, making threshold inclusivity explicit. Tests check returned values, not actual WPF panel visibility.

blocks.title: Invalid work width differs from unset requested geometry
blocks.explanation: Zero, negative, NaN and positive-infinity work widths must throw; those are invalid available spaces, not missing preferences. By contrast NaN requested size/coordinates are allowed and normalize to desired width, fitted height and centered coordinates, yielding 1240 by 1016 at 340,12 in a 1920-by-1040 area. The test matrix does not independently exercise every invalid work coordinate or extreme finite arithmetic case.
